outcome: maternal outcomes (duration of second stage, risk of cesarean delivery, contraction abnormalities, maternal complications)
neonatal outcomes (APGAR scores, hyperbilirubinemia, neonatal complications)
cohort: 100 women admitted with prelabour rupture of membranes beyond 36 weeks of gestation were enrolled and allotted to two groups.
finding: Labor induction with oxytocin for prelabour rupture of membranes beyond 36 weeks is associated with a longer second stage and higher risk of cesarean delivery for failure to progress compared to misoprostol, which was found to be effective, safe, and led to higher patient satisfaction with similar overall maternal and neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Labor induction with oxytocin infusion was associated with a higher risk of cesarean delivery for failure to progress compared to transvaginal misoprostol.
